sentences.text: List the matter for hearing in usual course.
Meanwhile, Registry is directed to call for records.

I.A.Nos.1 & 2 of 2023  I.A.No.1 of 2023 is filed by respondent/claimants seeking for direction to the appellant for depositing of the amount awarded by the Tribunal and I.A.No.2 of 2023 is filed for vacating the interim order dated 07.12.2022 passed by this Court in I.A.No.2 of 2022 in main appeal.
This is a case of death and the claimants filed M.V.O.P.No.98 of 2018 under Sections 163-A and 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.9,00,000/- along with interest.

The Tribunal after exhaustingly considering the evidence on record, held that the accident occurred due to deceased's own rash and negligence in driving the tractor owned by the 1st respondent, fixed liability on the 1st and 2nd respondents, who are owner and Insurance company and awarded an amount of Rs.12,82,600/- (Rupees Twelve Lakhs Eighty Two Thousand Six Hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.
Assailing the same, the Insurance company filed the present appeal.

In the appeal, it is contended that as the deceased himself was responsible for the accident and for his own negligence, the liability is to be fastened on him and it was rather a case of self negligence.
Considering the aforesaid submissions, this Court had initially passed interim orders staying the impugned Judgment.
The said interim order is now sought to be vacated.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimants submitted that the Tribunal, after evaluating the evidence and material on record, has ultimately determined liability on both the 1st and 2nd respondents.
The aspect as to whether the Insurance company has any liability or not can be decided while considering the main appeal on merits.

As already the claimants were successful in being awarded the compensation, and in regard to financial needs and interests, it is just and necessary for them to meet the benefit by receiving part of the compensation.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company, opposing the application, contended that in case the Insurance Company/appellant succeeds in the present appeal, any amounts, if permitted to be withdrawn by the claimants, would be difficult for them to recover.
Considering the rival submissions, this Court is of the view that it could be just and fair to allow the claimants to avail the benefit of partial withdrawal on condition of providing security.

In view of the same, the interim order earlier granted is modified to the extent of directing the Insurance Company/appellant to deposit half of the compensation awarded along with interest and costs within four (04) months from the date of receipt of the order and on such deposit being made,
the claimants are permitted to withdraw 50% of the amount so deposited on furnishing 3rd party security equivalent to value.
Accordingly, both applications stand disposed of.
